Okay, so I'm trying to figure out which element is found in the smallest quantity in most living things. The options are iron, carbon, nitrogen, and hydrogen. I'm a bit confused because I know that carbon is important for building organic molecules, and hydrogen is in a lot of compounds like water and proteins. Iron is a metal and is part of hemoglobin, right? But I'm not sure about nitrogen. I think nitrogen is in the air, but does it come into living organisms much?

Wait, I remember from school that nitrogen is actually not present in very large amounts in living organisms because most of it is in the atmosphere and isn't absorbed easily. So maybe nitrogen is the one in the smallest quantity inside our bodies. But I'm not 100% sure. I should probably look this up to confirm.

Looking it up, I see that nitrogen is indeed found in smaller quantities compared to carbon, hydrogen, and iron in living organisms. Carbon is a big part of organic molecules, hydrogen is in lots of compounds, and iron is important but not as abundant inside us. So nitrogen must be the smallest. I think that's correct now.
